newsitem.title: DUBAI: Islamic group condemns Israel's housing plan.
newsitem.headline: Islamic group condemns Israel's housing plan.

text.p: The secretary-general of the Organisation of Islamic Conference (OIC), the world's largest Moslem organisation, condemned on Friday plans by Israel to build new houses for Jews in Arab East Jeruslaem.

"Dr. Ezz al-Deen al-Iraqi expressed his deep concern over the dangereous situation in the city of Jerusalem as a result of Israel's decision to build a new settlement north of the holy city," a statement issued by the Jeddah-based group said.
"This illegal decision which contradicts with all international treaties and accords, demonstrates non-commitment on the part of Israel to the (Middle East) peace process," the statement added.
It said the secretary-general urged the international community to work towards forcing the Israeli government to reverse its decision.
The OIC groups more than 50 Moslem countries.
Israel on Wednesday said it would build 6,500 houses for Jews in Jabal Abu Ghneim or Har Homa.
Israel says all of Jerusalem is its capital. Palestinians consider Arab East Jerusalem, which Israel seized in the 1967 Middle East war, as the capital of a future Palestinian state.
